item.title: Mitochondrial DNA abundance is a determinant of immunogenic cell death in cancer.
item.author: Tanaka K, Adachi Y, Irie T, Yamamori-Morita T, Kumagai K, Owari T, Okumura G, Kobayashi Y, Bando H, Tsukada Y, Kumagai S, Itahashi K, Sugiyama E, Izumi H, Shibata Y, Goto K, Ohashi A, Kobayashi SS, Koyama S, Nishikawa H.
item.description:
Cells experiencing mitochondrial stress can undergo apoptosis or cell death that triggers innate immune activation. We examined the mechanisms determining these distinct outcomes in cancer. Abundant mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and high expression of the cGAS-STING pathway were features of KRAS-mutant cancers. In a pharmacological screen, MEK inhibitor (MEKi) effectively induced mtDNA release into the cytosol in KRAS-mutant cancer cells. However, MEKi also induced PRKN-mediated mitophagy, which limited mtDNA release by eliminating damaged mitochondria. Inhibition of mitophagy sustained mtDNA efflux and amplified cGAS-STING signaling. Mechanistically, PRKN-mediated mitophagy restrained mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) to limit mtDNA efflux. item.title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity.
item.author: Zhou JA, Tu J, Yue J, Zhang QE, Chen Y, Fan Q, Ma J, Zuo Y, Liu NN, Cheng J, He J.
item.description:
Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1 + T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. item.title: T cell cross-priming by PD-L1<sup>+</sup> type 1 conventional dendritic cells mediates the antitumor efficacy of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody.
item.author: Luri-Rey C, Rodríguez I, Arrieta-Aranzueque S, Guillamón DR, Vercher E, Soria N, Molero-Glez P, Cuesta R, Gomis G, Azpilikueta A, Bolaños E, Manzanal A, Garasa S, Kaisho T, Alexandru R, Domínguez PP, Calvo A, Exposito F, Heras-Murillo I, Sancho D, Capello M, Pencheva N, Berraondo P, de Andrea C, Jure-Kunkel M, Teijeira Á, Melero I.
item.description:
Bispecific antibodies that conditionally engage costimulatory receptors aim to enhance antitumor T cell immunity while limiting systemic toxicity. We investigated mechanisms underlying the clinical performance of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody. Therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1×4-1BB was largely independent of PD-L1 expression on malignant cells but waned in Batf3 -/- mice or upon depletion of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1-specific deletion of PD-L1 markedly limited tumor control. PD-L1×4-1BB enhanced proliferation of tumor-antigen-specific CD8 + T cells through mechanisms dependent on cross-presentation, the presence of interleukin (IL)-12, 4-1BB costimulation, and CD40L-mediated cDC1 licensing. item.title: PD-L1 expression in germinal centers promotes humoral immunity by restricting T follicular regulatory cell differentiation.
item.author: Akama-Garren EH, Zhang Y, Heesters BA, Fallon PG, Carroll MC.
item.description:
Germinal center (GC) responses generate humoral immunity through coordinated interactions between B cells and T follicular helper (TFH) and T follicular regulatory (TFR) cells. Despite high expression of PD-1 by TFH and TFR cells, the function of its ligand PD-L1 in the GC is unclear. Here, we show an immunogenic role for PD-L1 via tuning T-B collaboration to promote humoral immunity. Integrated analyses of secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) revealed that B cell zone reticular cells (BRCs), including follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), expressed PD-L1. BRC expression of PD-L1 facilitated GC formation and enabled loss of B cell tolerance in autoantibody disease. Mechanistically, BRC-specific deletion of PD-L1 enhanced TFH cell production of Sostdc1 and TFR cell differentiation, destabilizing T-B contacts in the GC. item.title: A microbiome-reactive TMIGD2<sup>hi</sup> Th17 subset is spatially enriched at the intestinal epithelium and expanded in inflammatory bowel disease.
item.author: Pedersen TK, Jain T, Segerstolpe Å, Lin C, Shih AR, Yuan L, Ashenberg O, Kaper ME, Twardus SW, Ricciardi R, Lau H, Moon JJ, Brix S, Xavier RJ, Graham DB.
item.description:
Subsets of intestinal CD4 + T cells directly recognize commensal bacteria and coordinate tolerance versus protective immunity. Our limited understanding of CD4 + T cell specificities and corresponding functional phenotypes has created a barrier to deciphering the mechanisms of mucosal homeostasis and inflammation mediated by the adaptive immune system. To address this, we leveraged an immunodominant Bacteroidetes epitope in SusC to perform single-cell profiling of the SusC-specific and total CD4 + T cell landscapes in intestinal tissues of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). By analyzing phenotypes and T cell receptor specificities in parallel, we uncovered phenotypic diversification of T helper 17 (Th17) cells in IBD and identified an epithelial-localized, SusC-reactive Th17 subset that is BACH2 lo , GZMA hi , and expresses the costimulatory receptor TMIGD2. item.title: Human brain cellular xenografts in neuroimmunology and beyond.
item.author: Fattorelli N, Martinez-Muriana A, Perry VH, Mancuso R.
item.description:
Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. item.title: NF-κB phosphorylation controls enhancer selection to shape the inflammatory gene program.
item.author: Leão FB, Bhatt D, Vaughn L, Liao W, Maloney D, Guichard V, Hampton B, Yang A, Postler TS, Yang-Fischer R, Zhao J, Farber D, Ghosh S.
item.description:
Inflammatory transcriptional responses mediated by NF-κB are diverse despite similar upstream activation signals. Because phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65 promotes interaction with co-activators CREB-binding protein/E1A binding protein p300 (CBP/p300) and selectively affects gene expression, we asked whether this modification distinguishes regulatory architectures underlying distinct immune functions. In macrophages carrying a Rela Ser276Ala mutation, p65 phosphorylation at serine 276 (S276) was dispensable for NF-κB binding to primed enhancers but essential for recruitment to nucleosome-occluded regions lacking pre-bound transcription factors (TFs) and activating histone marks. Such latent enhancers required phosphorylated NF-κB to recruit CBP/p300, promote histone acetylation, and open chromatin. item.title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation.
item.author: Ginhoux F, Mulder K, Arcila-Barrera S, Amit I.
item.description:
Macrophages are among the most versatile differentiated cell types in the body, serving as key regulators of tissue development, homeostasis, inflammation, repair, and immunity. Their functional diversity cannot be captured by fixed subsets, binary activation states, or single-marker definitions. Macrophage identity emerges instead from the integration of developmental origin, tissue niche, epigenetic history, local environmental cues, and disease-associated signals. Advances in single-cell genomics, spatial profiling, epigenomics, in vivo perturbation, and computational modeling now show that this behavior is organized through modular gene programs, so that any given macrophage state is best described as a weighted combination of program activities rather than a discrete label. item.title: Lactate dehydrogenase A-dependent redox control of selective mRNA translation directs monocyte fate commitment.
item.author: Yang N, He H, Liu X.
item.description:
Monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation is a central process that shapes immune responses across diverse contexts, yet how inflammatory cues engage metabolism to instruct monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Here, using a CRISPR-based metabolic screen combined with monocyte-specific perturbations in bacterial lung infection, we identified lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) as a key metabolic regulator of monocyte commitment to the nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2) + macrophage fate in vivo. LDHA-dependent cytosolic nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) regeneration enabled selective hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1α) translation through its 5' untranslated region (UTR) and is associated with structural remodeling of this region. item.title: Skin-resident CXCR6<sup>+</sup> memory CD4<sup>+</sup> T cells and dendritic cells form dermal perivascular hubs that drive relapse in allergic dermatitis.
item.author: Asahina R, Minami F, Nakamizo S, Miyake T, Yonekura S, Kogame T, Kanameishi S, Katsuo K, Irie H, Nakajima S, Nomura T, Kitoh A, Egawa G, Kabashima K.
item.description:
CD4 + tissue-resident memory T (T RM ) cells are crucial for relapse in allergic skin conditions. However, the mechanisms underlying their maintenance and pathogenic potential remain poorly defined. Here, across multiple models of allergic dermatitis, we identified a C-X-C chemokine receptor 6 (CXCR6 + ) subpopulation within CD4 + T RM cells as a distinct pathogenic subset that rapidly induces relapse. This subset is supported by C-X-C chemokine ligand 16 (CXCL16)-dependent interactions with CD301b + conventional type 2 dendritic cells (cDC2s) for in situ maintenance. Functional blockade of the CXCL16-CXCR6 signaling pathway impaired proliferation and maintenance of CXCR6 + CD4 + T RM cells.
